statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. NQ trades 29,434.50, +0.61%, 30.25 points below a 29,464.75 session high, having widened the post-FOMC reopen range to 29,247.75-29,464.75 without once returning to the low. A second consecutive hour of unretraced extension is genuine shallow-pullback structure and moves Tail from 18 to 20, into the watch band. It stops there because the entire leg spans 0.74% on roughly 20k contracts, because it recovers Wednesday's Fed-day decline rather than breaking into new territory, and because the cross-asset stack is diverging rather than aligning: WTI has fallen to $101.55 after Washington indicated the damaged Saudi East-West pipeline will restart within days, VIX closed at 17.71, and the 10-year sits at 5.01% with the 2-year at 4.738%. Tail remains well below the block threshold.
recommendation: The step from 18 to 20 is paid for by observation rather than assumption. The 29,247.75 low has now survived two full hours untested while price added roughly 90 points and continued to hold within 30 points of the session high; that is the shallow-pullback signature a mean-reversion basket is most exposed to, and it warrants the watch band. Three factors keep it from going further. The move is 0.74% of index value in the thinnest liquidity of the day. It retraces a decline rather than extending a trend into new territory. And the amplifier stack is weakening rather than building, with the crude supply premium unwinding on the reported pipeline restart and volatility pricing subdued at a 17.71 VIX close. The mapped danger window covers 12:30 to 14:30 UTC, spanning the jobless claims, housing starts and Philadelphia Fed block at 12:30 UTC and the cash open at 13:30 UTC, where the overnight leg meets real liquidity for the first time. Forecast Tail peaks at 23 across that window, still inside the watch band, because no post-release path has been observed.
headline: NQ extends to 29,434.50 with the 29,247.75 reopen low untested, lifting Tail to 20 and the watch band while a 5.01% 10-year and $101 crude keep Stress high
body:
The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3-3/4 to 4 percent at 18:00 UTC on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, the first increase in three years, judging that economic activity is expanding at a solid pace while inflation remains elevated. Chair Kevin Warsh framed the decision as supporting a timelier return to the 2 percent goal, and projections pointed to at least one further increase this year. Cash markets closed split on the day: the Dow fell about 1.2%, the S&P 500 lost 0.4%, and the Nasdaq-100 finished at 28,945.06, up 0.02%, after a 28,753.29-29,235.89 range. The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.01%, its highest since 2007, with the 2-year up more than seven basis points to 4.738%. VIX rose 2.97% to 17.71 off an intraday 16.40-18.94 range.

Since the Globex reopen the futures path has been one-directional. NQ has traded 29,247.75-29,464.75 and now sits at 29,434.50, 30.25 points under the high, with the low untested across two consecutive assessment hours. That unretraced extension is the single piece of evidence moving Tail higher; everything around it is stabilising. WTI has fallen to $101.55, down 0.86% on the day and well off the $104.89 print earlier in the session, after the United States said the Houthi-damaged Saudi East-West pipeline would restart within days, unwinding part of the supply premium that had carried crude above $107 Brent. Latest-session breadth context is mixed rather than aligned: megacaps split five up and three down with a -0.11% mean, semiconductors were firmer at +0.82% mean on Intel's 4.03% gain amid reported SK Hynix memory-fab discussions, while software and communication services lagged.

The next scheduled catalysts are the 12:30 UTC block of initial jobless claims, housing starts, building permits and the Philadelphia Fed index, followed by the 13:30 UTC cash open. Consensus is near 205k claims, 1.320M housing starts against a 1.239M prior, and a Philadelphia Fed reading near 31.3 after 47.4. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was only partially collected for this run, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so futures levels and the calendar were sourced independently.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 published Claude hours cover a complete FOMC cycle. The state opened at Tail 14 in the low band through the Asian and European sessions of 16 September, holding 13-16 with a normal dominant mode and no observed directional structure. It stepped into the watch band at 12:00 UTC with the US pre-market, running 20-22 through the early afternoon as positioning built into the decision, and reached 24 in the 18:00 UTC statement hour. The single orange print came at 19:00 UTC, Tail 31 with a trend-down mode, during the press conference and the yield-led equity leg that took the Dow down roughly 600 points. That resolved quickly: 20 by 20:00 UTC as the whipsaw two-sided, then 18 and 16 as cash closed and volatility decayed, before 18 with a trend-up mode at 23:00 UTC once the reopen leg began. All 24 hours are available from published history and none has been restated with later information.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 20 for the current hour, the only slot backed by observed price-path structure, and eases through the Asian session to an 18 trough between 04:00 and 06:00 UTC as the unretraced leg ages out of its liquidity window. It firms to 19 across the European pre-open and cash open, where continental desks price the hike and a 5.01% 10-year in cash for the first time, then steps to 20 in the hour before the US data block. The 12:00 to 14:00 UTC slots carry the highest conditional readings at 22, 23 and 23, spanning the 12:30 UTC claims, housing starts and Philadelphia Fed release and the 13:30 UTC cash open; the mapped danger window matches that span at 12:30 to 14:30 UTC. No slot reaches the block threshold, because a post-release continuation path is conditional and has not been observed. The path then decays through the US afternoon to 19, lifts to 20 for the 20:00 UTC power hour on rebalancing flow, and settles at 17-18 overnight. Stress stays in the high band throughout, easing from 70 to a 65-66 overnight floor and peaking at 73 across the event hours, while Confidence declines from 87 to 66 as the horizon extends beyond observed evidence.
